source_limitations: Source observations from publisher-owned web search excerpts on 2026-10-28; not a full-page authenticated human review, not exact-sense independent CEFR signoff. Four Cambridge A2 matches (raincoat, toothache, bookshelf, postcard); two Cambridge B1 conflicts (saucepan, dustbin); six unlabelled Cambridge senses (washcloth, shoelace, lunchbox, doormat, bathrobe, sunscreen), with a separate Collins COBUILD B2 lead for sunscreen. These are provisional editorial leads, not proof of CEFR placement or Myanmar accuracy. No release, no audio/device test.

shortlist_snapshot.english_definition: A coat made to keep rain from soaking your clothes.
shortlist_snapshot.myanmar_meaning: မိုးရေမစိုစေရန် ဝတ်ဆင်သော မိုးကာအင်္ကျီ
shortlist_snapshot.example_sentence: I packed a raincoat because the forecast warned of heavy rain.

records.independent_reviewer_task: A2 British Essential rain-protection noun sense aligns with the provisional garment definition; independently verify the Myanmar phrase and example.

shortlist_snapshot.english_definition: Pain in a tooth or in the area around a tooth.
shortlist_snapshot.myanmar_meaning: သွားတစ်ချောင်း သို့မဟုတ် သွားပတ်ဝန်းကျင်တွင် ဖြစ်သော သွားကိုက်ဝေဒနာ
shortlist_snapshot.example_sentence: He missed football practice because his toothache became worse.

records.independent_reviewer_task: Cambridge A2 tooth pain noun supports the general meaning; confirm whether countability and the original football example are natural in British English.

shortlist_snapshot.english_definition: A shelf used for storing or displaying books.
shortlist_snapshot.myanmar_meaning: စာအုပ်များ တင်ထားရန် ပြုလုပ်ထားသော စာအုပ်စင်
shortlist_snapshot.example_sentence: I put the new dictionary on the highest bookshelf.

records.independent_reviewer_task: Cambridge Learner A2 physical shelf sense aligns; independently verify the Myanmar gloss and original sentence.

shortlist_snapshot.english_definition: A small card that can be mailed with a short message, often showing a picture.
shortlist_snapshot.example_sentence: We sent a postcard to our grandparents from the seaside.

records.independent_reviewer_task: Cambridge A2 postcard meaning aligns; review whether the draft definition's short-message condition is unnecessarily restrictive.

shortlist_snapshot.english_definition: A deep cooking pan with a handle, often used for boiling food.
shortlist_snapshot.myanmar_meaning: အစားအစာပြုတ်ရန် အသုံးပြုသော လက်ကိုင်ပါ အိုးငယ်
shortlist_snapshot.example_sentence: Heat the milk gently in a saucepan before adding the chocolate.

records.independent_reviewer_task: Cambridge labels the exact deep cooking pan sense B1, versus draft A2. Require independent A2 exact-sense justification or replacement/retiering; do not silently relabel.

shortlist_snapshot.english_definition: A container used for collecting rubbish before it is taken away.
shortlist_snapshot.example_sentence: Put the empty packet in the dustbin near the kitchen door.

records.independent_reviewer_task: Cambridge labels the UK household outdoor large rubbish bin B1, while the draft A2 definition describes any rubbish container and the example is by a kitchen door. Confirm physical referent and level; consider UK bin versus dustbin distinction.

shortlist_snapshot.english_definition: A small piece of cloth used for washing the face or body.
shortlist_snapshot.myanmar_meaning: မျက်နှာ သို့မဟုတ် ကိုယ်ခန္ဓာ သန့်စင်ရာတွင် သုံးသော အဝတ်စငယ်
shortlist_snapshot.example_sentence: He used a clean washcloth to wipe his face after the match.

records.independent_reviewer_task: Cambridge marks washcloth US and gives UK facecloth/flannel. The British-focused syllabus needs independent lexical choice, exact-sense CEFR and Myanmar gloss review; no CEFR label was observed.

shortlist_snapshot.english_definition: A thin cord used to fasten a shoe.
shortlist_snapshot.myanmar_meaning: ဖိနပ်ကို ချည်တင်းစေရန် အသုံးပြုသော ဖိနပ်ကြိုး
shortlist_snapshot.example_sentence: Tie your shoelace before you run across the playground.

records.independent_reviewer_task: Cambridge lists the shoe-fastening noun usually in plural. The singular draft is grammatical in context but verify natural British usage; no CEFR label observed.

shortlist_snapshot.english_definition: A small container used to carry food for a midday meal.
shortlist_snapshot.myanmar_meaning: နေ့လယ်စာ ထည့်ယူသွားရန် အသုံးပြုသော ထမင်းဘူး
shortlist_snapshot.example_sentence: She put a sandwich and an apple in her lunchbox before school.

records.independent_reviewer_task: Cambridge describes a box for carrying lunch; no CEFR level observed. Do not infer A2 merely from everyday familiarity; review Myanmar and example.

shortlist_snapshot.english_definition: A small mat placed by a doorway for wiping shoes.
shortlist_snapshot.myanmar_meaning: တံခါးဝတွင် ဖိနပ်သုတ်ရန် ခင်းထားသော ဖျာ
shortlist_snapshot.example_sentence: Please wipe your shoes on the doormat before entering.

records.independent_reviewer_task: Cambridge separates the literal floor mat from figurative person who accepts mistreatment; draft uses literal mat. No CEFR level observed; do not confuse the senses.

shortlist_snapshot.english_definition: A loose piece of clothing worn after a bath or shower.
shortlist_snapshot.myanmar_meaning: ရေချိုးပြီးနောက် ဝတ်ဆင်လေ့ရှိသော အပေါ်ထပ်ဝတ် အင်္ကျီရှည်
shortlist_snapshot.example_sentence: He put on a warm bathrobe after taking a shower.

records.independent_reviewer_task: Cambridge gives dressing gown as a related term; distinguish post-bath towelling robe from British dressing gown and independently source A2 exact-sense level.

shortlist_snapshot.english_definition: A cream or lotion that protects skin from sunlight.
shortlist_snapshot.myanmar_meaning: နေရောင်ခြည်ဒဏ်မှ အရေပြားကို ကာကွယ်ပေးသော လိမ်းဆေး
shortlist_snapshot.example_sentence: Apply sunscreen before spending the afternoon at the beach.

records.independent_reviewer_task: Cambridge Learner gives the skin-protection product sense without an observed CEFR label. Collins COBUILD marks sunscreen B2; independent editor must reconcile this against draft A2 before retention.
